walkthroughs.body_html:
Family — a core area of GCSE Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Family brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Family.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Giddens called modern relationships 'pure' because they:
options: Are monogamous
Continue while rewarding to both
Are religious
Last for life

A reconstituted family is a family living in temporary housing.
A reconstituted family is one that has been put back together after divorce.
A family formed when partners with children from previous relationships come together — a 'blended' or step-family — one of several family forms recognised in family diversity literature.

mcqs.q: What did Murdock claim about the nuclear family?
options: Reliable research is published in journals; valid research isn't.
It is the only valid family form and others are dysfunctional.
It is universal and performs four essential functions in all societies.
It is a recent invention of capitalism.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between reliability and validity in research?
options: It is a recent invention of capitalism.
Reliable and valid mean the same thing — that the research is good.
Reliability is whether a method produces consistent results when repeated; validity is whether it actually measures what it claims to. A method can be reliable but invalid, or valid but unreliable.
Reliable research is published in journals; valid research isn't.
